summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and long-standing anemia was admitted for malaise and worsening abdominal pain. She was found to have severe anemia with a hemoglobin of 4.3 g/dL and received three units of packed red blood cells. A CT scan showed no active gastrointestinal bleeding but confirmed diverticulosis. Her anemia was attributed to vitamin B12 deficiency and possible myelodysplastic syndrome, leading to initiation of B12 injections. Congestive heart failure symptoms worsened post-transfusion but improved with IV furosemide. Warfarin was resumed given no evidence of bleeding. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient hematology follow-up, continued B12 replacement, and management of chronic conditions.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Diverticulosis of large intestine without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Presence of left artificial hip joint
